content: A home of one's own is best, even if small; a man is master in his own hall.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Bú er betra, þótt lítit sé (Hávamál, Stanza 36) — Poetic Edda
explanation: A tiny cottage with thatched walls and two goats may look humble to the arrogant, but within its borders you answer to your own conscience and bend the knee to no patron. Dependency on another person's bread corrodes dignity; honest self-sufficiency is the bedrock of peace.
practicalInsight: Value and protect your personal independence today. Take pride in what you have built with your own hands, however modest.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your life have you surrendered your autonomy in exchange for comfortable subservience?
